summary: A 1950 L-6 live-in cab on a granite point above the Kern River in Sequoia National Forest; unstaffed, closed to visitors, and still used as a radio repeater.

facts.design: 14x14 ft live-in L-6 cab on an open timber tower about 20 ft tall

access.note: CalWild describes a hiking trail to the lookout. Fire-lookouts.org (last updated 2013) says the structure is not staffed and is closed to the public, and NHLR says the cab is used only in emergencies. No source describes a visitor entry arrangement.

visit.trail_note: Hike of 2-3 miles round trip from a parking area at about 7,500 ft (CalWild). Fire-lookouts.org calls the trail overgrown and puts it at two miles from the parking area to the lookout, about four miles round trip. Forest roads 24S15 and 23S16 are often closed; check with the Western Divide Ranger District.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Sequoia National Forest, Hot Springs Ranger District

events.note: Sequoia National Forest announced a planned lookout station on Baker Ridge to replace the one on Sunday Peak; a trail was to be built first

Peakbagging.com says the first structure on the site was built in 1942. A 1942 newspaper report said a temporary structure would be erected before the August 21 manning date. Fire-lookouts.org dates the first cab on maps to about 1943
One-room wooden cabin beside the tower, built as living quarters; NHLR suggests it may have served the Aircraft Warning Service in WWII
Reconstruction of the Baker Point Trail reported as nearing completion
Current L-6 lookout; NHLR gives 1950 and Peakbagging.com says probably 1950; fire-lookouts.org says 1950s. NHLR says two mules were killed during construction
Peakbagging.com says the lookout has been closed since 1986
Fire Lookout Evaluation Report by Mark Thornton gave 24 points for historical significance, which fire-lookouts.org says made it eligible for the National Register

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Peakbagging.com says the first structure was built in 1942, and a 1942 newspaper report says a temporary structure would be erected. Fire-lookouts.org says maps indicate a first 7x7 cab around 1943. The current lookout is dated to 1950 by NHLR, probably 1950 by Peakbagging.com, and 1950s by fire-lookouts.org.

NHLR gives 7,490 ft (2,283 m) for the lookout, the figure in the record. Fire-lookouts.org gives 7,754 ft for the lookout, CalWild gives 7,754 ft for the summit, Peakbagging.com gives 7,760 ft, and a 1946 newspaper gives 8,500 ft for the lookout on Baker Mountain. A 1941 report gave 7,944 ft for the planned Baker Ridge station.
NHLR calls the cab a BC-301 type. Fire-lookouts.org calls it a C-3-L or L-6 live-in building. The record uses L-6, which fire-lookouts.org also gives.

notes_for_editor: Construction dates conflict for the first structure (1942 vs about 1943) and the current tower is 1950 in most sources. Status data is thin: the fire-lookouts.org page was last updated in 2013 and Peakbagging.com's closure date (1986) has no other source. No source read gives a current visitor policy for the cab. Elevations differ by about 260 ft depending on whether the lookout or the summit is meant. Fire-lookouts.org credits its cost and historic-eligibility points to a 1988 report that was not read directly. Trail length conflicts: CalWild gives 2-3 miles round trip; fire-lookouts.org gives two miles from the parking area to the lookout (about four miles round trip). The story gives both.
